title: Paintings
subject: History (CDS/NDA)

blocks.heading: 🎨 Painting Traditions of India
blocks.intro: From ancient cave murals to royal miniature schools and tribal folk paintings.

blocks.heading: 1. Murals & Miniatures
bullets: Mural Paintings: Giant paintings done on walls/rocks. Prominent at Ajanta Caves (Jataka tales, Fresco technique - painting on wet plaster) and Bagh.

Miniature Paintings: Small, detailed paintings on paper or palm leaves. - *Mughal School:* Introduced court scenes, portraits, hunting scenes. Reached peak under **Jahangir**. - *Rajput School:* Focused on religious themes (Radha-Krishna, Ramayana) and courtly lives. E.g., Kangra, Basohli, Kishangarh (famous painting *Bani Thani*).

blocks.heading: 2. Folk Paintings
bullets: Madhubani Paintings (Bihar): Mithila region. Traditionally done by women using rice paste, twigs, fingers, and natural dyes. Displays nature, birds, fish, and deities. Has geographical indication (GI) tag.

Warli Paintings (Maharashtra): Tribal art using basic geometric shapes (triangles, circles, squares) made of white paste (rice flour) on mud/ochre walls, showing daily activities, crop cycles, and tarpa dance.
Pattachitra (Odisha): Scroll paintings on cloth or dried palm leaves. Displays tales of Lord Jagannath and Krishna.

formulas: Ajanta: Buddhist murals | Miniatures peak: Jahangir | Madhubani: Bihar | Warli: Maharashtra
